email.subject1: signals HR Acuity isn't acting on
email.body1:
Austen, saw HR Acuity launched the Trust & Risk Statement and joined the Workday Innovation Partner Program this year.

A new framework plus a Workday tie-in opens a lot of accounts, and in RevOps the bottleneck is rarely leads, it's signal-to-action latency: in-market accounts surface faster than the team can route and touch.

I built a personalized signal play for HR Acuity off your hiring and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing them tend to progress ~4.4x faster, with 3-5x more meetings per rep and no new headcount. Worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?
email.body2:
Austen, quick follow-up for HR Acuity.

Most RevOps teams lose pipeline in the handoff: a signal fires from the Workday ecosystem or inbound, then sits for days before anyone touches it. That latency is measurable and usually the gap between a booked meeting and a dead account.

I'd walk you through a teardown of your current outbound, three specific changes to the signal-to-touch flow. Our best practices alone tend to lift response rates 50-70%. Want to grab 15 minutes so I can show you?
email.body3:
Austen, last bit of proof for HR Acuity.

Memgraph had more in-market accounts than the team could touch and couldn't hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, every email auto-logged to their CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how HR Acuity's reply rate likely compares to other HR-tech teams. Want to hop on a quick call and I'll walk you through it?
email.body4:
Austen, I'll stop reaching out on this one, but didn't want to leave you empty-handed.

If tightening signal-to-action latency isn't a priority this quarter, no problem at all. I know a new partner program and a category launch swallow a RevOps roadmap fast.

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a one-page playbook of three AI-SDR plays scoped to your motion? I'll tailor it to HR Acuity either way.
